subject: Tyrannosaurus rex
fact: T. rex had powerful jaws and teeth shaped for tearing meat.

subject: Triceratops
fact: Triceratops had three facial horns and a large bony frill.

subject: Stegosaurus
fact: Stegosaurus had large plates along its back and spikes on its tail.

subject: Brachiosaurus
fact: Brachiosaurus had longer front legs than back legs, giving its body a sloping shape.

subject: Apatosaurus
fact: Apatosaurus was a huge long-necked plant eater with a whip-like tail.

subject: Diplodocus
fact: Diplodocus had an extremely long tail and a small head compared with its body.

subject: Velociraptor
fact: Velociraptor was a feathered predator about the size of a large turkey.

subject: Ankylosaurus
fact: Ankylosaurus was covered in bony armor and had a heavy tail club.

subject: Spinosaurus
fact: Spinosaurus had a tall sail on its back and a long crocodile-like snout.

subject: Allosaurus
fact: Allosaurus was a large meat-eating dinosaur with three-fingered hands.

subject: Carnotaurus
fact: Carnotaurus had two horn-like bumps above its eyes and very short arms.

subject: Dilophosaurus
fact: Dilophosaurus had two thin crests on top of its head.

subject: Parasaurolophus
fact: Parasaurolophus had a long hollow crest that may have helped make sounds.

subject: Iguanodon
fact: Iguanodon had a pointed thumb spike on each hand.

subject: Pachycephalosaurus
fact: Pachycephalosaurus had a thick dome of bone on top of its skull.

subject: Gallimimus
fact: Gallimimus had long legs and a beak-like mouth and could probably run quickly.

subject: Deinonychus
fact: Deinonychus had a large curved claw on each foot.

subject: Oviraptor
fact: Oviraptor had a toothless beak and was closely related to feathered dinosaurs.

subject: Therizinosaurus
fact: Therizinosaurus had enormous hand claws and probably ate mostly plants.

subject: Compsognathus
fact: Compsognathus was a small lightweight dinosaur with long legs.

subject: Giganotosaurus
fact: Giganotosaurus was one of the largest known meat-eating dinosaurs.

subject: Albertosaurus
fact: Albertosaurus was a close relative of T. rex that lived earlier in time.

subject: Ceratosaurus
fact: Ceratosaurus had a horn on its snout and bony ridges above its eyes.

subject: Corythosaurus
fact: Corythosaurus had a tall helmet-shaped crest on its head.

subject: Maiasaura
fact: Maiasaura nested in colonies and cared for young in nesting grounds.

subject: Edmontosaurus
fact: Edmontosaurus was a large duck-billed dinosaur with rows of grinding teeth.

subject: Kentrosaurus
fact: Kentrosaurus had plates near its shoulders and long spikes farther down its back.

subject: Styracosaurus
fact: Styracosaurus had a nose horn and several long spikes around its frill.

subject: Protoceratops
fact: Protoceratops was a smaller horned dinosaur with a parrot-like beak.

subject: Euoplocephalus
fact: Euoplocephalus was an armored dinosaur with a tail club.

subject: Argentinosaurus
fact: Argentinosaurus was one of the largest land animals known from fossils.

subject: Saltasaurus
fact: Saltasaurus was a long-necked dinosaur with small bony plates in its skin.

subject: Amargasaurus
fact: Amargasaurus had two rows of tall spines along its neck.

subject: Plateosaurus
fact: Plateosaurus was an early long-necked plant eater that lived during the Triassic Period.

subject: Coelophysis
fact: Coelophysis was a slim fast-moving predator from the Late Triassic.

subject: Herrerasaurus
fact: Herrerasaurus was one of the earliest large predatory dinosaurs.

subject: Archaeopteryx
fact: Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings as well as teeth and a long bony tail.

subject: Microraptor
fact: Microraptor was a small feathered dinosaur with flight feathers on all four limbs.

subject: Pteranodon
fact: Pteranodon was a flying reptile with a long head crest and no teeth.

subject: Quetzalcoatlus
fact: Quetzalcoatlus was a gigantic pterosaur with a wingspan similar to a small airplane.

subject: Dimorphodon
fact: Dimorphodon was an early pterosaur with a large head and two different kinds of teeth.

subject: Mosasaurus
fact: Mosasaurus was a giant marine reptile that lived in the oceans of the Late Cretaceous.

subject: Plesiosaurus
fact: Plesiosaurus had a long neck, small head, and four paddle-like flippers.

subject: Ichthyosaurus
fact: Ichthyosaurus was a dolphin-shaped marine reptile that swam with powerful tails and fins.

subject: Liopleurodon
fact: Liopleurodon was a large short-necked marine reptile with strong jaws.

subject: Dunkleosteus
fact: Dunkleosteus was an armored fish with sharp bony jaw plates instead of normal teeth.

subject: Megalodon
fact: Megalodon was an enormous extinct shark known from its giant fossil teeth.

subject: Woolly Mammoth
fact: Woolly mammoths had long curved tusks and thick coats for cold climates.

subject: Smilodon
fact: Smilodon was a saber-toothed cat with very long upper canine teeth.

subject: Megatherium
fact: Megatherium was a giant ground sloth that could stand on its hind legs.

subject: Glyptodon
fact: Glyptodon was an armored mammal related to modern armadillos.

subject: Dire Wolf
fact: Dire wolves were large Ice Age predators that lived in the Americas.

subject: Dodo
fact: Dodos were flightless birds that once lived on the island of Mauritius.

subject: Titanoboa
fact: Titanoboa was a gigantic prehistoric snake that lived in warm tropical wetlands.

subject: Sarcosuchus
fact: Sarcosuchus was a huge crocodile-like reptile that lived alongside dinosaurs.

subject: Dimetrodon
fact: Dimetrodon had a tall sail on its back and lived before the dinosaurs.

subject: Edaphosaurus
fact: Edaphosaurus was an early plant eater with a tall sail along its back.

subject: Megaloceros
fact: Megaloceros was a giant deer with enormous antlers.

subject: Woolly Rhinoceros
fact: Woolly rhinoceroses had thick fur and lived in cold Ice Age environments.

subject: Terror Bird
fact: Terror birds were large flightless predators with powerful beaks and long legs.
